---
title: "Internals: the behavioral spec"
description: "How the Epic Online Services SDK behaves under the hood, interface by interface — the specification EOS Reimagined is built from."
---

This section is the project's **technical documentation**: how the Epic Online Services SDK behaves under the hood, written up interface by interface so the library can be (and is being) reimplemented cleanly. It is a *behavioral spec* — control flow, state, the async model, and the peer-to-peer wire protocol — not a line-by-line copy of anyone's code.

If you are here to *use* EOS Reimagined rather than hack on it, start with the [user guide](../../users/getting-started.qmd) instead.

## Start here

- [**Architecture**](architecture.qmd) — the core runtime: handles, singletons, bootstrap, the callback/frame async engine, settings.
- [**Network protocol**](protocol.qmd) — the peer-to-peer wire protocol (protobuf messages + transport). The interop contract two instances must share.
- [**ADR 0001 — Authenticated mesh identity**](adr/0001-authenticated-mesh-identity.qmd) — the design record for key-derived identities and the Noise XX channel every connection runs.
- [**Progress manifest**](progress.qmd) — the working status ledger for all interfaces (the polished summary lives on the [roadmap](../../users/roadmap.qmd)).

## Operational design

- [**Alpha tracing & config contract**](alpha-tracing.qmd) — the `eosr.json` / `EOSR_*` config resolution rules and the versioned JSON-Lines trace schema the diagnostics tooling agrees on.
- [**Export-surface census**](export-surface-census.qmd) — our exported EOS surface measured against the real Epic SDK.
- [**EOS Reimagined Manager**](manager.qmd) — the Windows/Linux plan for Steam discovery, safe SDK installation/restoration, managed instances, configuration, launching, and diagnostic runs.
- [**External social companion**](companion-client.qmd) — the planned out-of-process replacement for the social overlay's join surface.

## Reading it alongside the official material

These pages describe *observed behavior*. The authoritative ABI is the vendored headers in
[`include/eos/`](https://github.com/anishgoyal1108/EOS-Reimagined/tree/main/include/eos), and
Epic's public [EOS SDK documentation](https://dev.epicgames.com/docs/epic-online-services) and
[API reference](https://dev.epicgames.com/docs/api-ref) remain the best description of what a
*game developer* was promised. When the three disagree, the headers win — and the disagreement
is worth recording here.

## A note on how this was written

This documentation was produced by static analysis of a compiled EOS SDK emulator plus Epic's public SDK headers, cross-referenced where possible against surviving open-source prior art (see the credit in the project [README](https://github.com/anishgoyal1108/EOS-Reimagined#acknowledgments)). It exists so contributors can build a clean, portable implementation from an understood specification.
